<Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez>: In May 2025, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) launched the Make Onshoring Great Again Portal, a free tool designed to help small businesses identify U.S. manufacturers and producers. The database provides links to four private lists or directories, which are: IndustryNet, Thomasnet, Connex, and IQS directory.
• IndustryNet is an industrial marketplace
search engine operating since 1912 that lists more than
350,000 suppliers of machinery parts, supplies, and
services.\1\
\1\SBA Onshoring Portal, https://www.sba.gov/about-sba/priorities/ american-manufacturers/make-onshoring-great-again-portal/.
• Thomasnet is a longstanding industrial
platform operating for over 120 years that helps small
and medium businesses connect with more than 500,000
American manufacturers and suppliers by location and
company size.\2\ Some businesses have raised concerns
on Reddit that it operates as a pay-to-play model,
where they have to bid for viability, however, the
option on the SBA website is a free basic model.
\2\Id.
• CONNEX Marketplace connects U.S.
manufacturers and suppliers into a searchable supply
chain solution.\3\ NIST utilizes CONNEX Marketplace to
help regional Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP)
centers locate specific suppliers and fulfill
government supply chain requests. The Department of
Defense's Office of Local Defense Community Cooperation
utilizes customized versions of the platform to map
defense manufacturing capabilities and ensure national
security in military supply chains.
\3\Id.
• The IQS Directory is an online business-to-
business industrial directory, which was founded in
2000. It connects original equipment manufacturer (OEM)
buyers and engineers with industrial suppliers,
fabricators, and distributors across the U.S. and
Canada.\4\
\4\SBA Onshoring Portal Directory, https://www.iqsdirectory.com/ madeinamerica/.
The Committee noted several challenges with H.R. 9718 as introduced. The SBA currently has an onshoring platform on its website, however, the Committee has limited data regarding its utilization, effectiveness, and whether it is necessary for Congress to codify. While the Portal is relatively new, the underlying data is not. The SBA does not own or manage the databases, raising concerns that the information may become outdated or stale. Additionally, although access to the Portal is free, some of the third-party platforms it relies on offer higher-tier paid models. The Committee remains concerned about the SBA's reliance on the Office of Advocacy (Advocacy) for updates and improvements to the portal and feels that the legislation is blurring the lines of independence between the SBA and Advocacy. With that said, Advocacy, under the leadership of former Acting Administrator of the SBA, Mr. Everett Woodell (January-February 2025), indicated that it has no issues with the SBA seeking input from the Chief Counsel. Given these concerns the Committee has negotiated a compromise, which will be offered as an amendment in the nature of a substitute (ANS).
Nydia M. Velazquez,
Ranking Member.
